provisions.topic_title: Section 49(1) read with Section 47(i): Capital Gains on Assets Acquired via HUF Partition & Previous Owner Rules
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
# Statutory Provisions: Capital Gains on Assets Acquired upon HUF Partition

> [!NOTE] Statutory Framework Overview
> When an asset is distributed on total or partial partition of a Hindu Undivided Family (HUF), no immediate tax liability arises. The statutory framework ensures tax continuity by stepping into the shoes of the previous owner when the recipient member subsequently transfers the asset.

---

### 1. Statutory Non-Transfer Character | Section 47(i)
Under **Section 47(i)** of the Income-tax Act, 1961, any distribution of capital assets on the **total or partial partition of an HUF** is explicitly excluded from the definition of 'transfer'.
- **Taxability at Partition:** Nil (No capital gain tax is levied on the HUF or the coparcener/member at the time of partition).
- **Legal Status:** It is considered a division of pre-existing rights among members rather than an alienation of property.

---

### 2. Cost of Acquisition | Section 49(1)(i)
Where a capital asset becomes the property of an assessee under a partition of an HUF, the cost of acquisition of the asset to the assessee is deemed to be:
- **Deemed Cost:** The **cost for which the previous owner (the HUF)** acquired it.
- **Cost of Improvement:** Any cost incurred by the previous owner as well as the assessee for capital improvements is deductible under **Section 55(1)(b)**.

| Transaction Stage | Cost to be Adopted | Relevant Statutory Provision |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Acquisition by HUF | Cost paid by HUF | Section 49(1)(i) |
| Partition of HUF | Exempt from Transfer | Section 47(i) |
| Improvement by Member/HUF | Actual Expenditure | Section 55(1)(b) |
| Subsequent Transfer | Full Value of Consideration | Section 48 |

---

### 3. Determination of Period of Holding | Section 2(42A)
To determine whether the asset is Long-Term Capital Asset (LTCA) or Short-Term Capital Asset (STCA):
- **Explanation 1(i)(b) to Section 2(42A):** The period for which the asset was held by the **previous owner (HUF)** must be included in the period of holding of the member/coparcener.
- **Asset Classification Threshold (Immovable Property):** Held for more than **24 months** (inclusive of HUF holding period) = Long-Term Capital Asset.

---

### 4. Computation Mechanism | Section 48
Upon subsequent transfer of the capital asset by the member, the taxable capital gain is calculated as follows:


   Full Value of Consideration Received / Accruing
Less: Expenditure Incurred Wholly & Exclusively in Connection with Transfer
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
= Net Sale Consideration
Less: Cost of Acquisition (Cost to Previous Owner u/s 49(1))
Less: Cost of Improvement (Incurred by Previous Owner & Assessee u/s 55(1)(b))
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
= Taxable Long-Term / Short-Term Capital Gain


> [!IMPORTANT] Key Principle on Improvement Costs
> Any capital expenditure incurred on improvements to the property by either the previous owner (HUF) or the current owner (assessee) after its acquisition is fully deductible from the Net Sale Consideration under Section 55(1)(b).

provisions.topic_title: Cost of Acquisition for Inherited Property and Clearance of Pre-existing Encumbrances under Section 49(1) & Section 48
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
# Statutory Provisions & Judicial Principles: Capital Gains on Inherited Encumbered Property

## 1. Cost of Acquisition in Cases of Inheritance / Will [Section 49(1)]

Where a capital asset becomes the property of the assessee under a gift, will, succession, inheritance, or distribution of assets on partition of a HUF:

* **Deemed Cost of Acquisition:** The cost of acquisition of the asset to the assessee shall be deemed to be the **cost for which the previous owner acquired it**.
* **Period of Holding:** The period of holding of the previous owner is included to determine whether the asset is Short-Term Capital Asset (STCA) or Long-Term Capital Asset (LTCA) as per Section 2(42A).

> [!NOTE]
> **Definition of Previous Owner:** "Previous owner of the property" in relation to any capital asset owned by an assessee means the last previous owner of the capital asset who acquired it by a mode of acquisition other than those referred to in Section 49(1).

---

## 2. Discharge of Encumbrance: Judicial Precedent & Principles

The statutory treatment of loan repayment/mortgage clearance depends on **who created the mortgage**:

| Parameters | Pre-Existing Mortgage Created by Predecessor | Mortgage Created by Successor (Assessee) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Created By** | Previous owner prior to transfer/inheritance. | Current assessee after acquiring title. |
| **Nature of Right Passed** | Successor gets an **encumbered title** / defective title. | Successor gets an unencumbered title, then encumbers it. |
| **Purpose of Payment** | To discharge encumbrance and acquire a **clear, marketable title**. | To discharge personal borrowing/obligation. |
| **Tax Treatment** | Eligible as **Cost of Acquisition / Improvement** under Section 48 / 55(2). | **NOT eligible** as Cost of Acquisition / Improvement. Treated as mere application of income. |
| **Supreme Court Authority** | *RM. Arunachalam v. CIT [1997] 227 ITR 222 (SC)* | *CIT v. V. Indira [1979] 119 ITR 837 (Mad)* / *RM. Arunachalam* |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **The Supreme Court Benchmark (*RM. Arunachalam v. CIT*):**
> Where a property is inherited subject to a mortgage created by the previous owner, the successor inherits only the equity of redemption. Therefore, when the successor pays off the mortgage debt created by the predecessor to release the mortgage deed and secure absolute title, such payment is directly attributable to the acquisition of full ownership rights and qualifies as part of the total Cost of Acquisition under Section 48.

---

## 3. Computation Framework for Inherited Encumbered Asset


  Full Value of Consideration (Sale Price)
  LESS: Expenses incurred wholly and exclusively in connection with Transfer
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Net Sale Consideration
  LESS: Cost of Acquisition
        (a) Original Cost to Previous Owner [u/s 49(1)]
        (b) Amount paid by Successor to discharge Pre-existing Mortgage [u/s 48 / 55(2)]
  LESS: Cost of Improvement (if any)
  ----------------------------------------------------------------------
  Capital Gains (Short-Term / Long-Term)


> [!WARNING]
> **Self-Created Encumbrances Trap:** If the assessee mortgages an inherited property *after* inheriting it to obtain a personal bank loan, clearing that mortgage before sale does NOT increase the cost of acquisition. That clearance is merely an application of sale proceeds to discharge a personal liability.

provisions.topic_title: Cost of Acquisition for Original and Bonus Shares (Pre vs Post 01-04-2001)
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
| Asset Category | Period of Acquisition / Allotment | Statutory Provision | Cost of Acquisition (CoA) Determination |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Original Equity Shares** | Prior to 01-04-2001 | Sec 55(2)(b)(i) | Higher of **Actual Cost of Acquisition** or **FMV as on 01-04-2001** |
| **Bonus Shares** | Prior to 01-04-2001 | Sec 55(2)(b)(i) Proviso | **FMV as on 01-04-2001** (Option to substitute FMV available) |
| **Bonus Shares** | On or After 01-04-2001 | Sec 55(2)(aa)(ii) | **NIL** (Zero statutory cost) |
| **Transfer Expenditure** | Date of Transfer | Sec 48(i) | Fully deductible from Full Value of Consideration (e.g., Brokerage on sale) |

### Core Statutory Rules
- **Brokerage Treatment**: Brokerage paid at acquisition forms part of purchase cost; brokerage paid at transfer is deductible under Section 48(i) to arrive at Net Sale Consideration.
- **Pre-2001 FMV Benchmark**: For any asset acquired prior to 01-04-2001, the assessee has the statutory option to step up the cost to the Fair Market Value as of 01-04-2001.
- **Post-2001 Bonus Exclusion**: Bonus shares issued on or after April 1, 2001 cannot take the FMV benefit and must be valued at ₹0.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Bonus Shares Pre vs Post 2001 Cut-off**: The benefit of FMV substitution as of 01-04-2001 applies to bonus shares allotted prior to 01-04-2001 because the asset was held on April 1, 2001. For post-2001 bonus shares, Section 55(2)(aa)(ii) strictly mandates a zero cost of acquisition.

provisions.topic_title: Capital Gains: Right Shares & Right Entitlement Taxability
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Matrix: Taxation of Right Entitlements & Shares

| Asset Type | Statutory Reference | Cost of Acquisition (Sec 55(2)(aa)) | Period of Holding (Sec 2(42A)) |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Original Shares** | Sec 55(2)(aa)(i) | Actual Cost / FMV as on 01.04.2001 | From original date of acquisition |
| **Right Entitlement (Renounced)** | Sec 55(2)(aa)(ii) | **NIL** (entire consideration is taxable) | Date of offer to date of renouncement |
| **Right Shares (Subscribed)** | Sec 55(2)(aa)(iii) | Amount paid to the company | From date of allotment by company |
| **Right Shares (Acquired by Renouncee)** | Sec 55(2)(aa)(iv) | Purchase price of Entitlement + Amount paid to company | From date of allotment by company |

### Key Statutory Checklists

- **Renouncement Benchmark**: The renouncement of a right entitlement creates an immediate Capital Asset transfer under Section 2(14). Since cost is NIL, 100% of consideration forms Short-Term Capital Gains (STCG).
- **Period of Holding Classification**: Unlisted equity shares require a holding period exceeding 24 months to qualify as Long-Term Capital Assets (LTCA). Listed shares require a holding period exceeding 12 months.

> [!IMPORTANT] Statutory Trap for Renounced Entitlements: The period of holding for Right Entitlements ALWAYS starts on the date the company offers the rights and ends on the date of renouncement. It NEVER relates back to the acquisition date of the original shares.

3. Consideration received ONLY via share allotment. | Transaction is **NOT treated as a transfer**.
No capital gains tax at succession. | | **Section 47A(3)**
Recapture Rule | Any condition under Sec 47(xiv) breached within 5 years of succession. | Exemption withdrawn; capital gains taxed in hands of company in year of breach. | | **Section 49(1)**
Cost of Acquisition | Asset acquired by company under Section 47(xiv) transaction. | Cost to company = **Cost to previous owner** (sole proprietor). | | **Section 2(42A)**
Period of Holding | Asset acquired under Section 47(xiv) exemption mechanism. | Holding period of previous owner **included** in total period. | ### Core Statutory Checklists * **Section 47(xiv) Exemption Criteria:** * Complete business succession where 100% assets and liabilities transition to the company. * Proprietorship consideration strictly restricted to share capital allotment without any monetary/non-monetary boot. * **Section 49(1) & Section 2(42A) Tacking Principles:** * Cost basis remains anchored to original acquisition cost incurred by the proprietor. * Immovable property holding period includes proprietor's tenure (exceeding 24 months results in Long-Term Capital Asset). > [!WARNING] Statutory Recapture Trap (Section 47A(3)) > If the proprietor's shareholding drops below 50% voting power within 5 years from succession, the capital gains exempted earlier under Section 47(xiv) become taxable in the hands of the successor company in the year of default.

provisions.topic_title: Demerger Tax Framework: Section 47 Exemption, Cost Allocation & Section 54F Integration
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
| Aspect | Statutory Provision | Operative Threshold / Condition | Legal Tax Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Demerged Company Transfer** | Section 47(vib) | Resulting company must be an Indian company | Not regarded as transfer; exempt from Capital Gains tax |
| **Shareholder Allotment** | Section 47(vid) | Issue of shares by resulting company in consideration of demerger | Not regarded as transfer; no immediate tax liability |
| **Cost Allocation (Resulting Co.)** | Section 49(2C) | Net book value of transferred assets ÷ Net worth before demerger | Applied to original Cost of Acquisition in demerged company |
| **Cost Reduction (Demerged Co.)** | Section 49(2D) | Original cost of shares in demerged company less Section 49(2C) cost | Adjusted Cost of Acquisition of original shares |
| **Period of Holding** | Section 2(42A)(g) | Aggregate holding period of demerged company shares + resulting company shares | Determines status as Long-term Capital Asset |
| **Exemption on Sale** | Section 54F | Net consideration reinvested in 1 residential house in India | Exemption available on LTCG on subsequent sale |

### Key Statutory Conditions & Rules
* **Continuity of Shareholding:** Section 47 does not mandate shareholders to retain resulting company shares for any minimum post-demerger period to preserve corporate tax immunity.
* **Section 54F Reinvestment Timelines:** Purchase within 1 year before or 2 years after transfer, or construct within 3 years after transfer of the Capital Asset.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Net Worth Definition for Section 49(2C): Net worth means the aggregate of paid-up share capital and general reserves as appearing in the books of account of the demerged company immediately before the demerger.

provisions.topic_title: Section 32, Section 43(6) & Section 50: Block of Assets Depreciation and Capital Gains
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
| Statutory Provision | Legal Scope | Triggering Condition | Tax Consequence / Formula |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 43(6)** | Written Down Value (WDV) | Aggregate of Opening WDV + Additions − Net Sale Consideration | Closing WDV of the Block |
| **Proviso to Sec 32(1)** | Restricted Depreciation | Asset acquired & put to use for < 180 days in the Previous Year | Restricted to 50% of prescribed rate |
| **Section 50(1)** | Short-Term Capital Gain | Net Consideration > (Opening WDV + Cost of Additions) | Excess taxed as STCG; Depreciation = Nil |
| **Section 50(2)** | Empty Block Determination | All assets in the block transferred during the Previous Year | WDV > Consideration → STCL; Consideration > WDV → STCG |

### Statutory Principles Checklist
- **Block Existence Test**: Capital gains under Section 50 arise ONLY IF sale consideration exceeds (Opening WDV + Additions) OR all assets in the block are transferred.
- **Depreciation Priority Rule**: If the block WDV is positive and includes assets put to use for less than 180 days, 50% restricted depreciation applies first to the extent of the acquisition cost of such new assets.

> [!IMPORTANT] Zero Depreciation Rule: When Section 50 is triggered due to full transfer of assets or sale consideration exceeding block value, no depreciation is allowable under Section 32 for that assessment year.

provisions.topic_title: Section 45(1A) & Section 50: Insurance Compensation for Destruction of Depreciable Capital Assets
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Insurance Receipts for Damaged/Destroyed Assets

| Section / Statutory Provision | Statutory Condition / Trigger | Year of Taxability | Full Value of Consideration & Tax Treatment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 45(1A)** | Receipt of money or asset from insurer due to flood, fire, explosion, riot, or enemy action | Previous Year in which money/asset is **actually received** | Money received or Fair Market Value of asset received |
| **Section 48** | Computation of Capital Gains mechanism | Year of Receipt (via Sec 45(1A)) | Consideration minus Cost of Acquisition / Indexed Cost / WDV |
| **Section 50** | Destruction/transfer of Depreciable Assets forming part of a block | Year of Receipt (via Sec 45(1A)) | Excess consideration over WDV + Additions is deemed **Short-Term Capital Gain (STCG)** |

### Core Statutory Rules

* **Deemed Transfer & Taxability Year:** Under Section 45(1A), capital gains arise upon damage/destruction, but chargeability is deferred strictly to the **Previous Year of receipt** of insurance money or asset.
* **Deemed Consideration:** Under Section 48, the amount of money or Fair Market Value of the asset received from the insurer is treated as the **Full Value of Consideration**.
* **Depreciable Assets Mechanism:** Under Section 50, any capital gain arising from the transfer or destruction of depreciable assets is mandatorily treated as **Short-Term Capital Gain** (or Short-Term Capital Loss if the block ceases to exist).

> [!IMPORTANT] Statutory Benchmark: Section 45(1A) vs General Transfer Rules
> Although destruction of an asset is not a voluntary transfer under Section 2(47), Section 45(1A) creates a statutory fiction making insurance compensation taxable exclusively under Capital Gains in the year the money/asset is received.

provisions.topic_title: Section 45(2): Conversion of Capital Asset into Stock-in-Trade
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
# Statutory Framework: Conversion of Capital Asset into Stock-in-Trade

### Statutory Summary Matrix

| Head of Income | Statutory Section | Consideration / Valuation Base | Year of Taxability |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Capital Gains** | Section 45(2) | Fair Market Value (FMV) on conversion date | Previous Year in which Stock-in-Trade is sold/disposed |
| **PGBP** | Section 28 | Sale Proceeds minus FMV on conversion date | Previous Year in which Stock-in-Trade is sold/disposed |

### Core Statutory Conditions & Mechanics

- **Deemed Transfer**: Under Section 2(47)(iv), the conversion or treatment of a Capital Asset as Stock-in-Trade constitutes a statutory transfer in the Previous Year of conversion.
- **Taxability Deferral**: Although transfer occurs in the year of conversion, Capital Gains tax is deferred and charged to tax only in the Previous Year in which such Stock-in-Trade is actually sold or otherwise transferred.
- **Bifurcation Mechanism**: Total gain is split into two components:
  1. **Capital Gain** = FMV on Conversion Date − Cost / Indexed Cost of Acquisition.
  2. **Business Profits (PGBP)** = Actual Sale Proceeds − FMV on Conversion Date.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Indexation & Holding Period Cut-Off**  
> The Period of Holding and Indexation Benefit (if applicable) are determined strictly up to the **date/year of conversion**, NOT the year of actual sale. However, tax payment obligation remains deferred until the year of sale.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 45(2): Conversion of Capital Asset into Stock-in-Trade & Section 54EC Relief
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
# Section 45(2) & Section 54EC: Conversion of Capital Asset into Stock-in-Trade

### Master Statutory Summary Matrix

| Statutory Provision | Triggering Event / Condition | Deemed Consideration / Valuation | Year of Taxability |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 2(47)(iv)** | Conversion of capital asset into stock-in-trade | FMV on date of conversion | Transfer occurs in the year of conversion |
| **Section 45(2)** | Actual sale or transfer of converted stock-in-trade | FMV on conversion date = Full Value of Consideration | Deferred to the Previous Year of actual stock sale |
| **Section 28 (PGBP)** | Realization of converted stock-in-trade | Sale Proceeds minus (FMV on conversion date + Development Costs) | Taxed as Business Income in year of stock sale |
| **Section 54EC & CBDT Circular 791** | Investment in specified long-term assets within 6 months | Max deduction cap: ₹ 50 Lakhs per Financial Year | 6-month period reckoned from date of stock sale |

### Core Statutory Rules

* **Deferral Mechanism (§ 45(2)):** Though transfer occurs upon conversion under Section 2(47)(iv), capital gains tax liability arises only in the year when stock-in-trade is actually sold.
* **Proportionate Chargeability:** If stock-in-trade is sold partially across multiple years, capital gains are recognized **proportionately** based on the ratio of stock sold in that year.
* **PGBP Income Computation:** Business profits equal Sale Consideration minus (FMV on conversion date + Cost of construction/development).
* **CBDT Circular No. 791 (02.06.2000):** For Section 54EC exemption in Section 45(2) cases, the 6-month investment period is calculated from the **date of sale of stock-in-trade**, not the date of conversion.

> [!WARNING] Statutory Ceiling Trap under Section 54EC
> The maximum exemption under Section 54EC for long-term capital gains arising in any single financial year cannot exceed **₹ 50 Lakhs**, irrespective of whether investments are made across one or two financial years.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 45(5): Compulsory Acquisition & Enhanced Compensation
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Section 45(5) Compulsory Acquisition

| Type of Compensation | Statutory Section | Year of Taxability | Full Value of Consideration | Cost of Acquisition & Deductions |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Initial Compensation** | Section 45(5)(a) | Previous Year in which compensation is **first received** | Initial compensation awarded or determined | Cost of Acquisition / Indexed Cost + Transfer Expenses under Section 48 |
| **Enhanced Compensation** | Section 45(5)(b) | Previous Year in which enhanced amount is **actually received** | Enhanced compensation received | Cost of Acquisition = **NIL**; Deduction allowed for litigation expenses incurred |
| **Reduction by Court** | Section 45(5)(c) | Rectified for the Previous Year of original assessment | Recomputed consideration | Assessment amended under Section 155(16) |

#### Key Statutory Conditions & Rules
* **Deferment of Taxability**: Although transfer occurs in the year of compulsory acquisition, Section 45(5)(a) shifts the tax incidence to the Previous Year of actual receipt of initial compensation.
* **Character of Enhanced Gain**: Enhanced compensation retains the original character of capital gain (Long-Term Capital Gain or Short-Term Capital Gain) based on the original holding period.
* **Interim Court Orders**: Any enhanced compensation received against an interim court order is taxable only in the Previous Year in which the final order is passed.

> [!IMPORTANT] Cost of Acquisition for Enhanced Compensation
> Cost of Acquisition is always taken as **NIL** for enhanced compensation because the entire original Cost of Acquisition is fully claimed against the initial compensation under Section 45(5)(a).

provisions.topic_title: Section 10(37): Exemption on Compulsory Acquisition of Urban Agricultural Land
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Framework: Section 10(37) Exemption Matrix

| Assessment Scenario | Eligible Assessee | Mode of Transfer | Preceding 2-Year Ag. Use | Section 10(37) Status | Tax Treatment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Urban Ag. Land Compulsory Acquisition | Individual / HUF | Compulsory Acquisition | Yes (by self/parents/HUF) | **Fully Exempt** | Nil Capital Gains Tax |
| Voluntary Sale of Urban Ag. Land | Individual / HUF | Voluntary Sale | Yes / No | **Inapplicable** | Taxable Capital Gains u/s 45 |
| Urban Ag. Land (No Ag. Use) | Individual / HUF | Compulsory Acquisition | No | **Inapplicable** | Taxable Capital Gains u/s 45(5) |
| Corporate / Company Owned Land | Company / Firm | Compulsory Acquisition | Yes / No | **Inapplicable** | Taxable in Hands of Entity |

### Core Statutory Conditions Checklist
- **Eligible Assessee**: Exemption is exclusively restricted to an **Individual** or a **Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)**.
- **Asset Qualification**: Must be an **urban agricultural land** specified in Section 2(14)(iii).
- **Mandatory Use Test**: Land must be used for agricultural purposes during the **preceding 2 years** from the date of transfer by the individual, parent, or HUF.
- **Transfer Type**: Capital gain must arise from **compulsory acquisition** under any law, or transfer where consideration is determined by Central Government / RBI.

> [!IMPORTANT] Year of Taxability on Failure of Exemption
> Where Section 10(37) conditions are not satisfied, capital gains on compulsory acquisition are taxable under Section 45(5) in the Previous Year in which initial compensation is **first received**.

> [!WARNING] Statutory Exclusions
> Section 10(37) benefit is **strictly unavailable** for voluntary sales, non-agricultural land, or corporate assessees (Companies, LLPs, Firms).

provisions.topic_title: Taxation on Liquidation of Company: Deemed Dividend u/s 2(22)(c), Shareholder Capital Gains u/s 46(2) & Exemption Limits u/s 54EC
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
| Head / Provision | Statutory Section | Operative Condition / Threshold | Tax Treatment & Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Company Hand Tax** | Section 46(1) | Distribution of assets to shareholders upon liquidation | Not regarded as transfer for Section 45; No Capital Gains tax on company |
| **Deemed Dividend** | Section 2(22)(c) | Distribution attributable to accumulated profits (capitalized or not) prior to liquidation | Taxable under Income from Other Sources in hands of shareholder |
| **Shareholder Capital Gains** | Section 46(2) | Money / FMV of assets received minus Deemed Dividend u/s 2(22)(c) | Deemed Full Value of Consideration (FVC); Capital Gains taxed u/s 48 |
| **Tax Rate (Unlisted Shares)** | Section 112 | Holding period exceeding 24 months | Taxable as Long-Term Capital Gain @ 12.5% |
| **Sec 54EC Exemption** | Section 54EC | Applicable only to land or building and actual transfers | Ineligible for shares and deemed transfers (CIT v. Ruby Trading Co.) |

### Core Statutory Checklists
- **Deemed Dividend Benchmark**: Extent of accumulated profits immediately before liquidation determines the Section 2(22)(c) portion.
- **Capital Gain Consideration Rule**: $\text{Full Value of Consideration} = \text{Total Distribution Received} - \text{Deemed Dividend u/s 2(22)(c)}$.
- **Section 54EC Restriction**: Exemption applies strictly to transfer of long-term capital asset being land or building, requiring actual statutory transfer.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Statutory Trap: Distribution on liquidation creates a dual tax effect for shareholders — dividend income up to accumulated profits under IFOS, and capital gains on the balance consideration.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 50B & Rule 11UAE: Capital Gains on Slump Sale and Net Worth Determination
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Master Statutory Summary Matrix

| Statutory Section / Rule | Legal Scope & Objective | Operative Threshold / Valuation Basis | Tax Impact / Statutory Treatment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 50B(1) & (2)** | Capital gains on Slump Sale | Undertaking held > 36 months (LTCG) vs ≤ 36 months (STCG) | Indexation benefit under Section 48 is **strictly prohibited**. |
| **Rule 11UAE** | Full Value of Consideration | Deemed FVC = Higher of **FMV1** (undertaking assets) or **FMV2** (consideration received) | Establishes statutory FMV benchmark for slump sale consideration. |
| **Sec 50B Explanation 1 & 2** | Computation of Net Worth | Depreciable assets at WDV u/s 43(6); Sec 35AD assets at NIL; Other assets at Book Value | Net worth acts as deemed **Cost of Acquisition** & **Cost of Improvement**. |
| **Section 32(1) Exp 5 & Sec 43(6)** | Mandatory Depreciation for WDV | Intangible assets (e.g. Patents @ 25%) must be reduced by eligible depreciation | WDV must be adjusted for tax depreciation even if omitted in financial accounts. |


### Statutory Checklists & Rules

* **Rule 11UAE FMV Determination**:  
  * **FMV1**: Stamp Duty Value for immovable property + Book value of other capital assets minus Book value of liabilities (excluding paid-up capital, revaluation reserves, and unprovided liabilities).  
  * **FMV2**: Value of monetary consideration plus FMV of non-monetary consideration received.  
* **Net Worth Computation Framework**:  
  * Total assets (WDV for depreciable assets + book value for non-depreciable assets) minus liabilities transferred.  
  * **Revaluation Reserve**: Revaluation of any asset must be **completely ignored** from both asset valuation and net worth.  


> [!WARNING] Statutory Trap: Mandatory Tax Depreciation
> Under Explanation 5 to Section 32(1), depreciation is mandatory. For computing net worth under Section 50B, depreciable assets must be taken at WDV computed under Section 43(6), irrespective of whether depreciation was actually claimed in the books of accounts.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 50B & Rule 11UAE: Slump Sale Taxation & Net Worth Computation
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Slump Sale Provisions

| Section / Rule | Statutory Subject | Operative Benchmark / Threshold | Tax Consequence / Treatment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 50B(1)** | Nature of Capital Gain | Undertaking held for > 36 months | Taxable as Long-Term Capital Gain (LTCG) |
| **Section 50B(2)** | Cost of Acquisition | Net worth of the undertaking transferred | Deemed Cost of Acquisition; No indexation allowed |
| **Rule 11UAE** | Full Value of Consideration | Higher of **FMV1** (Transferred Assets) or **FMV2** (Consideration Received) | Statutory Deemed Full Value of Consideration |
| **Sec 50B Expl. 1 & 2** | Net Worth Computation | Aggregate value of assets minus value of liabilities | Revaluation impact strictly excluded |


### Statutory Valuation Rules for Net Worth Assets

- **Depreciable Assets**: Valued at Written Down Value (WDV) of the block as per **Section 43(6)(c)**.
- **Capital Assets (100% Deduction)**: Valued at **NIL** if deduction claimed under Section 35AD.
- **Revalued Assets**: Revaluation reserve must be ignored; assets taken at original cost.
- **Other Assets**: Valued at book value as per the balance sheet.


### Formula for Deemed Consideration under Rule 11UAE

$$\text{Full Value of Consideration} = \max(\text{FMV}_1, \text{FMV}_2)$$

> [!IMPORTANT] 
> **No Indexation Benefit**: As per the second proviso to **Section 48** read with **Section 50B(2)**, benefit of indexation is strictly not available for computing capital gains on slump sale, even if the undertaking is a long-term capital asset.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 50B: Slump Sale Computation, Rule 11UAE Valuation & Section 47(iv) Holding-Subsidiary Exemption
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Slump Sale Mechanics & Group Restructuring Exemption

| Section / Rule | Statutory Scope & Condition | Valuation & Computational Rule | Legal & Tax Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 50B** | Slump sale of an undertaking for a lump sum consideration without itemized values. | Capital Gains = Deemed Full Value of Consideration − Net Worth of Undertaking. | Taxed in the year of transfer. **No indexation benefit** under Section 48. |
| **Rule 11UAE** | Determination of Full Value of Consideration for Section 50B slump sale. | **Higher of FMV1 or FMV2** (FMV1 = Assets at SDV/Book Value minus Liabilities). | Deemed Full Value of Consideration for Capital Gains computation. |
| **Section 43(6)** | Valuation of depreciable assets for computing Net Worth under Section 50B. | Aggregate asset value includes depreciable assets at **WDV as per Section 43(6)**. | Revaluation of assets strictly ignored; Section 35AD assets taken at **Nil**. |
| **Section 47(iv)** | Transfer of capital asset by Holding Co. to its **100% Indian Subsidiary**. | Entire capital asset transfer in corporate restructuring. | **Not a Transfer**: Complete exemption from Capital Gains tax. |
| **Section 47A** | Holding status drops below 100% or conversion into stock-in-trade within **8 years**. | Withdrawal of exemption previously granted under Section 47(iv). | Exempt Capital Gains become taxable in the year of contravention. |

### Statutory Checklists & Operational Rules

- **Net Worth Computation Rules (Section 50B Explanation 1 & 2)**:
  - **Depreciable Assets**: Take Written Down Value (WDV) of the block of assets under Section 43(6).
  - **Non-Depreciable Assets**: Take book value (strictly **ignore Revaluation Reserve / Revaluation impact**).
  - **Section 35AD Assets**: Value at **Nil** if 100% deduction was claimed.
  - **CA Audit Report**: Assessee must obtain and submit **Form 3CEA** electronically one month before the tax return due date.

- **Rule 11UAE Valuation Framework (FMV1 vs FMV2)**:
  - **FMV1**: Stamp Duty Value for Immovable Property + Book Value for Other Assets − Book Value of Liabilities.
  - **FMV2**: Value of monetary and non-monetary consideration received/accruing on transfer.

- **Tax Planning via Group Restructuring (Section 47(iv) & 47A)**:
  - Acquire **100% equity shareholding** prior to the date of transfer to make the restructuring **100% tax-free**.
  - **8-Year Lock-in**: Maintain 100% shareholding for at least **8 years** to avoid withdrawal of exemption under Section 47A.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Holding Period Threshold**: An undertaking held for **more than 36 months** qualifies as a Long-Term Capital Asset. However, indexation benefit under the second proviso to Section 48 is expressly denied under Section 50B(2).

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Sections 9B & 45(4): Tax Treatment on Reconstitution/Dissolution of Firm and Rule 8AB Attribution
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Sections 9B, 45(4) & Rule 8AB Framework

| Provision / Rule | Triggering Event | Consideration / Formula | Tax Head & Rate | Attribution / Relief |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 9B** | Dissolution or Reconstitution (Partner receives capital asset or stock-in-trade) | **Full Value of Consideration** = Fair Market Value (FMV) on date of receipt | Capital Gains or PGBP depending on nature of asset transferred | Net profit after tax credited to partner's capital account |
| **Section 45(4)** | Reconstitution of Firm (Partner receives money, capital asset, or both) | **Capital Gain (A)** = Money Received + FMV of Capital Asset - Adjusted Capital Account Balance | Charged in the hands of the specified entity as STCG / LTCG | Taxable gain attributed to remaining assets u/s 48(iii) read with Rule 8AB |
| **Rule 8AB / Section 48(iii)** | Capital gain charged u/s 45(4) on reconstitution | **Attribution Share** = Sec 45(4) Gain × (Asset Revaluation / Total Net Revaluation) | Deduction while computing Capital Gains on subsequent transfer | Reduces taxable capital gain on eventual sale of remaining assets |


### Core Statutory Checklist

- **Section 9B Mechanics:**
  - Taxable in the Assessment Year relevant to the Previous Year in which the asset is received by the specified person.
  - Cost of acquisition for computing gain u/s 9B is the actual cost or book value as per Income Tax provisions.

- **Section 45(4) Computation & Capital Account Adjustment:**
  - Capital account balance of the partner must be computed **after** giving effect to the profit/loss resulting from Section 9B deemed transfer.
  - Revaluation of assets or goodwill generation directly in books without tax realization is excluded while computing adjusted capital balance.

- **Rule 8AB Attribution & Subsequent Asset Sale:**
  - Capital gain u/s 45(4) attributed to depreciable or short-term assets is treated as Short-Term Capital Gain (STCG).
  - On subsequent sale of remaining assets, the attributed amount u/s 48(iii) is deducted from Full Value of Consideration.


> [!IMPORTANT] Interplay Between Section 9B and Section 45(4)
> Section 9B operates first as a deemed transfer of the specific asset handed over. The resulting net tax profit increases the retiring partner's capital balance. Section 45(4) then taxes any excess value (money + asset FMV) received beyond that updated capital balance.


> [!WARNING] Self-Generated Goodwill Taxability
> Under Section 55(2)(a), cost of acquisition of self-generated goodwill is **Nil**. However, if capital gain u/s 45(4) was previously attributed to goodwill under Rule 8AB, such attributed amount is deductible under Section 48(iii) upon its eventual sale.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 9B & Section 45(4): Reconstitution of Firm & Deemed Transfers
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### **Master Statutory Matrix: Reconstitution of Partnership Firm / Entity**

| Statutory Section | Triggering Event | Consideration / Value Basis | Head of Income & Taxability |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 9B** | Receipt of stock-in-trade or capital asset by partner/member on reconstitution or dissolution | **Fair Market Value (FMV)** of the asset on the date of receipt | **PGBP** (for stock-in-trade) or **Capital Gains** (for capital assets) in hands of entity |
| **Section 45(4)** | Receipt of money or capital asset by partner/member on reconstitution | Cash + FMV of capital asset received | **Capital Gains** in hands of entity on amount exceeding adjusted capital account balance |

---

### **Key Rules & Computation Checklist**

* **Deemed Transfer u/s 9B:**
  * **Stock-in-Trade:** Income = FMV of stock on receipt date minus Purchase Cost/Cost of Acquisition (Taxable under PGBP).
  * **Capital Asset:** Full Value of Consideration = FMV of capital asset on receipt date. Cost of acquisition determined u/s 48/55.

* **Deemed Capital Gains u/s 45(4):**
  * **Formula:** Taxable Gain $A = A_m + A_v - B$
    * $A_m$ = Money received by partner
    * $A_v$ = FMV of capital asset received by partner
    * $B$ = Adjusted balance in partner's capital account
  * **Negative Result:** If $A$ is negative, deemed taxable income under Section 45(4) is **Nil** (cannot be negative).

* **Capital Account Adjustment for Section 45(4):**
  * Capital account balance must be adjusted for the **net accounting profit/loss (post-tax)** arising to the firm on account of deemed transfers u/s 9B.

> [!IMPORTANT] Order of Application:
> Section 9B must ALWAYS be evaluated **first** to determine the tax liability and net accounting profit/loss of the firm. The partner's capital account balance is then updated with their share of post-tax profit/loss **before** computing capital gains under Section 45(4).

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Capital Gains: Pre-2001 Immovable Asset Valuation, Advance Money Forfeiture & Cost of Improvement
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Pre-2001 Capital Asset Provisions

| Provision / Section | Statutory Scope & Condition | Mandatory Tax Treatment / Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 55(2)(b) Proviso** | Immovable property acquired prior to 1st April 2001 | Option to adopt higher of Actual Cost or FMV as on 1st April 2001; **FMV capped at SDV** as on 1st April 2001. |
| **Section 51** | Advance money received & forfeited **prior to 1st April 2014** | **Deducted from Cost of Acquisition** (or substituted FMV) while computing Capital Gains upon subsequent transfer. |
| **Section 56(2)(ix)** | Advance money received & forfeited **on or after 1st April 2014** | Taxable directly under **Income from Other Sources (IFOS)**; NO reduction from Cost of Acquisition. |
| **Section 55(1)(b)** | Cost of Improvement incurred **prior to 1st April 2001** | **Completely ignored** and excluded from computation (absorbed in 01.04.2001 valuation). |


### Statutory Rule Checklists

* **Valuation Ceiling on 1st April 2001 Valuation**:  
  * **Formula**: $\text{Substituted Cost} = \text{Higher of } [\text{Actual Cost}, \text{Min}(\text{FMV as on 01.04.2001}, \text{SDV as on 01.04.2001})]$.  
  * **Land or Building**: Fair Market Value as on 1st April 2001 cannot exceed the Stamp Duty Value on that date.

* **Advance Money Forfeiture Rules**:  
  * **Pre-01.04.2014 Forfeiture**: Reduces effective Cost of Acquisition of the asset for future capital gains computation.  
  * **Post-01.04.2014 Forfeiture**: Taxed as revenue income in the year of forfeiture under Section 56(2)(ix).


> [!IMPORTANT]  
> **Statutory Trap - Pre-2001 Improvement Cost**: Any capital improvement expenditure incurred prior to 1st April 2001 must NEVER be added or indexed, as the asset's state and valuation as on 1st April 2001 already reflect all prior improvements.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 49(1) & Section 55: Cost of Acquisition & Advance Money Rules for Gifted Assets Acquired Prior to 1st April 2001
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Framework: Gifted Capital Assets Acquired Prior to 1st April 2001

| Section / Rule | Legal Provision | Condition / Ceiling | Tax Impact / Rule |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 49(1)** | Cost to Previous Owner | Asset acquired by gift, will, or succession | Deemed Cost of Acquisition = Cost to Previous Owner |
| **Section 55(2)(b)** | Option for FMV as on 01.04.2001 | Original acquisition prior to 1st April 2001 | Cost = Higher of Actual Cost OR Fair Market Value (FMV) as on 01.04.2001 |
| **Proviso to Sec 55(2)(b)** | Ceiling on FMV | SDV available as on 01.04.2001 | FMV as on 01.04.2001 **cannot exceed** Stamp Duty Value (SDV) as on 01.04.2001 |
| **Section 51** | Advance Money Forfeited | Forfeited prior to 1st April 2014 | Deductible ONLY if forfeited by **the assessee**. Forfeiture by **previous owner** is ignored |
| **Section 55(1)(b)** | Cost of Improvement | Capital additions after 01.04.2001 | Include expenditure incurred by previous owner and assessee after 01.04.2001 |


> [!IMPORTANT] Key Statutory Trap: Advance Money Forfeiture by Previous Owner
> Under **Section 51**, advance money retained prior to 1st April 2014 reduces the Cost of Acquisition ONLY when forfeited by the **assessee himself**. If the advance money was forfeited by the **Previous Owner**, it is treated as a capital receipt of the previous owner and **SHALL NOT** be deducted from the Cost of Acquisition when computing Capital Gains in the hands of the donee/successor.


#### Micro-Checklist for Cost Determination:
* **Step 1 (Base Cost):** Take actual cost to Previous Owner.
* **Step 2 (FMV vs SDV Cap):** Compare FMV as on 1st April 2001 with SDV as on 1st April 2001. FMV is restricted to SDV. Take higher of Actual Cost or Capped FMV.
* **Step 3 (Advance Money):** Ignore forfeiture by Previous Owner prior to 1st April 2014.
* **Step 4 (Cost of Improvement):** Add all capital improvement costs incurred on or after 1st April 2001 by previous owner and current owner.

provisions.topic_title: Section 54 & Section 51: Capital Gains Exemption & Forfeiture of Advance Money
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Section 51 & Section 54 Integrated Rules

| Provision / Section | Statutory Trigger / Condition | Tax Treatment / Formula | Judicial Benchmark / Landmark Rule |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 51** | Advance money forfeited prior to 01/04/2014 | Reduced from Cost of Acquisition | Reduces base cost before applying indexation |
| **Section 56(2)(ix)** | Advance money forfeited on or after 01/04/2014 | Taxed under *Income from Other Sources* | Does NOT reduce Cost of Acquisition |
| **Section 54** | Purchase/construction of residential house | Exempt = Lower of Capital Gain or Cost of New Asset | Purchase: 1 yr before or 2 yrs after transfer; Construction: 3 yrs after |
| **Section 54 Proviso** | Capital Gain ≤ ₹ 2 Crore (Once-in-a-lifetime) | Exemption available for **Two** residential houses in India | Aggregate investment across both houses is eligible |

### Core Statutory Checklist & Conditions

* **Forfeiture of Advance Money (Section 51 vs 56(2)(ix)):**
  * Any advance received and forfeited before 1st April 2014 must be deducted from the cost of acquisition of the capital asset.
  * Any advance forfeited on or after 1st April 2014 is treated as revenue income and charged under Section 56(2)(ix).

* **Ownership & Legal Title Requirement (Section 54):**
  * Execution of a registered sale deed is **not mandatory** to claim Section 54 exemption.
  * If the assessee pays full consideration and obtains possession under an agreement to sell, beneficial ownership is established (*Balraj v. CIT*).

> [!IMPORTANT] Dual House Property Exemption Threshold
> The option to claim Section 54 exemption for **two residential houses** is strictly restricted to cases where the long-term capital gain does not exceed **₹ 2 Crore**. This option can be exercised by an assessee only once in their lifetime.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 54: Exemption for Purchase of Integrated Adjacent Flats as One Residential House
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Framework: Section 54 Exemption & Unit Integration

| Statutory Provision | Core Condition / Requirement | Judicial Benchmark / Statutory Limit | Tax Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 54(1)** | Transfer of Long-Term Residential House and investment in new residential house | Purchase within 1 year before or 2 years after, or construction within 3 years | Exemption equal to investment made or Capital Gain, whichever is lower |
| **Integrated Flats Doctrine** | Purchase of multiple adjacent/contiguous flats modified into a single residential unit | Certified structural modification into one integrated unit (*CIT v. D. Ananda Basappa*) | Qualified as purchase of **one residential house** under Section 54 |
| **Section 54 Limit Proviso** | LTCG exceeding ₹ 2 Crore restricts exemption benefit to one residential house only | Maximum exemption capped at ₹ 10 Crore w.e.f. A.Y. 2024-25 | Benefit of two houses option unavailable if LTCG > ₹ 2 Crore |

### Key Judicial Benchmarks (*CIT v. D. Ananda Basappa*)

* **Integration Test:** Physical modification (e.g., opening interconnecting doors or removing dividing walls) certified by builder/architect proves intention to use as a single unit.
* **Irrelevant Factors:** Execution of separate sale deeds or prior occupation by different tenants before purchase does not alter the character of the integrated residential unit.

> [!IMPORTANT] Statutory Distinction: Two Separate Houses vs. One Integrated Unit
> Where LTCG exceeds ₹ 2 Crore, Section 54 restricts exemption to purchase of one residential house. However, if two adjacent flats are structurally unified into a single dwelling unit, it legally constitutes **one residential house**, satisfying the strict condition of Section 54(1).

provisions.topic_title: Section 45(5) & Section 54D: Capital Gains on Compulsory Acquisition of Industrial Asset
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
| Statutory Provision | Eligibility Criteria / Pre-condition | Statutory Window | Exemption / Tax Treatment |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 45(5)** | Compulsory acquisition of capital asset under any statutory law | Year of initial receipt | Chargeable to tax in the Financial Year in which compensation is first received |
| **Section 54D** | Land or building used for industrial undertaking for ≥ 2 years prior to transfer | 3 years after transfer date | Exempt to the extent of cost of new industrial land or building |

**Key Statutory Conditions for Section 54D Exemption:**

* **Prior Usage Test:** The land or building must have been used by the assessee for the purpose of an industrial undertaking for at least **2 years** immediately preceding the date of transfer.

* **Reinvestment Scope:** Assessee must purchase land/building or construct a building within **3 years** from the date of transfer for shifting, re-establishing, or setting up an industrial undertaking.

* **Exemption Quantum:** Exemption equals **Lower of Capital Gains** or **Cost of New Asset** acquired.

> [!IMPORTANT] Statutory Lock-in & Deferral Rule
> Capital gains tax liability is triggered in the year compensation is actually received under **Section 45(5)**. If the new asset under **Section 54D** is transferred within 3 years of purchase, its cost of acquisition will be reduced by the exemption previously claimed.

provisions.topic_title: Section 54F: Capital Gains Exemption on Transfer of Non-Residential Assets
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
# Statutory Summary: Capital Gains & Section 54F Exemption

### Master Statutory Framework Matrix

| Section | Subject / Aspect | Statutory Condition / Qualification | Tax Consequence / Formula |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 48** | Net Consideration | Gross Sale Consideration less Expenses incurred wholly & exclusively for transfer | Basis for computing Capital Gains & Exemption |
| **Section 54F(1)** | Asset Eligibility | Transfer of any Long-Term Capital Asset (LTCA) **other than** a residential house | Eligible for deduction from LTCG |
| **Section 54F(1)(a)** | Full Investment | Cost of New Residential House $\ge$ Net Consideration | **100% of Long-Term Capital Gain** is exempt |
| **Section 54F(1)(b)** | Partial Investment | Cost of New Residential House $<$ Net Consideration | Exempt LTCG = $\text{LTCG} \times \frac{\text{Cost of New House}}{\text{Net Consideration}}$ |


### Core Statutory Conditions Checklist

- **Eligible Assessee**: Exclusively an **Individual** or **Hindu Undivided Family (HUF)**.
- **Asset Transferred**: Must be a **Long-Term Capital Asset** other than a residential house (e.g., Jewellery, Shares, Land).
- **Timeline for Reinvestment**:
  - **Purchase**: Within **1 year before** or **2 years after** the date of transfer.
  - **Construction**: Within **3 years** after the date of transfer.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Ownership Disqualifications**: On the date of transfer, the assessee must **not own more than one residential house** (other than the new house). Furthermore, purchasing another house within 2 years or constructing another house within 3 years revokes the exemption.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Capital Gains: Section 50C Tolerance Limit, Section 55(2)(b) Pre-2001 Cost Ceiling, and Section 54 Exemption Cap
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Master Statutory Summary Matrix

| Section / Provision | Statutory Trigger / Condition | Operative Threshold / Limit | Tax Result / Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 50C** | Transfer of Land or Building or both | Stamp Duty Value $\le$ 110% of actual consideration | Actual sale consideration is treated as **Full Value of Consideration**. |
| **Section 55(2)(b)** | Asset acquired prior to **1st April 2001** | FMV as on **01.04.2001** restricted to SDV as on **01.04.2001** | Cost of Acquisition = Higher of Actual Cost and (FMV restricted to SDV). |
| **Section 54** | Transfer of Long-Term Residential House | Investment in 1 new residential house in India | Exemption available for purchase (1 yr before / 2 yrs after) or construction (3 yrs after). |
| **Section 54 Limit** | Statutory cap on Section 54 exemption | Maximum **₹ 10 Crores** cost of new asset / CGAS deposit | Exemption restricted to maximum **₹ 10 Crores**. Excess investment yields no deduction. |

---

### Key Statutory Checklists & Rules

#### 1. Section 50C: Stamp Duty Value Tolerance Rule
- **Safe Harbor Provision**: If the Stamp Duty Value determined by statutory authority does not exceed **110%** of the actual consideration received or accruing, the actual consideration shall be deemed to be the **Full Value of Consideration**.
- **Deemed Consideration Trigger**: If Stamp Duty Value exceeds **110%** of actual consideration, the Stamp Duty Value is taken as the **Full Value of Consideration**.

#### 2. Section 55(2)(b): Pre-2001 Asset Cost Determination
- **Base Cost Selection**: For assets acquired before **1st April 2001**, assessee can opt for Fair Market Value (FMV) as on **01.04.2001** in place of actual cost.
- **Stamp Duty Ceiling**: FMV as on **01.04.2001** cannot exceed the Stamp Duty Value (SDV) of the property as on **01.04.2001**, where SDV is available.

#### 3. Section 54: Exemption Scope & Statutory Limits
- **CGAS Deposit Scheme**: Amounts deposited in the **Capital Gain Account Scheme** before the due date of filing return under **Section 139(1)** are eligible for Section 54 exemption.
- **Monetary Cap of ₹ 10 Crores**: Effective from **Assessment Year 2024-25**, the maximum aggregate investment (purchase + construction + CGAS deposit) eligible for Section 54 exemption is capped at **₹ 10 Crores**.

> [!IMPORTANT] Pre-2001 FMV Benchmark Restriction:
> If Stamp Duty Value as on **01.04.2001** is available, the Fair Market Value as on **01.04.2001** CANNOT exceed such Stamp Duty Value. The benchmark cost is: Cost of Acquisition = Higher of Actual Cost and min(FMV as on 01.04.2001, SDV as on 01.04.2001).

> [!WARNING] Section 54 Exemption Ceiling:
> Any expenditure on purchasing/constructing a residential house or depositing in CGAS beyond **₹ 10 Crores** will NOT provide any additional tax relief under Section 54.

provisions.topic_title: Integrated Tax Computation: House Property Provisions, Deemed Consideration & Capital Gains Exemptions
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: House Property & Capital Gains Framework

| Head / Area | Statutory Provision | Operative Threshold / Statutory Condition | Tax Treatment / Legal Consequence |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **House Property** | **Section 23 & 24** | Higher of Expected Rent & Actual Rent; Municipal taxes deducted on actual payment basis. | Net Annual Value (NAV) less 30% Standard Deduction under Section 24(a) and actual interest under Section 24(b). |
| **Arrears of Rent** | **Section 25A** | Taxable in the year of receipt/realization, irrespective of property ownership. | Statutory deduction of 30% allowed; balance 70% taxable. |
| **Cost of Gifted Asset** | **Section 49(1)** | Asset acquired by gift, deed, or inheritance. | Cost of acquisition is deemed to be the cost to the **previous owner**. |
| **Deemed Consideration** | **Section 50C** | Stamp Duty Value (SDV) exceeds 110% of actual consideration. | **SDV is adopted** as the Full Value of Consideration. |
| **Reinvestment Exemption** | **Section 54** | Investment in residential house within 1 yr prior or 2 yrs post transfer. | Full exemption up to capital gains; **adjacent flats modified into one unit** qualify (*CIT v. Ananda Basappa*). |
| **Bonds Exemption** | **Section 54EC** | Investment in specified infrastructure bonds within 6 months (Max ₹ 50 Lakhs). | Exempt; **payment date governs eligibility** even if allotment occurs post 6 months (*Hindustan Unilever Ltd.*). |


### Micro-Checklist of Statutory Rules & Judicial Benchmarks

- **Municipal Taxes Deduction:** Deductible strictly on **actual payment basis** during the previous year, including payment of past arrears.
- **Adjacent Units under Section 54:** Two adjacent residential flats purchased under separate sale deeds and combined into a single residential unit qualify as **one residential house** (*CIT v. Ananda Basappa*).
- **Payment vs Allotment under Section 54EC:** Subscribing and making full payment within 6 months satisfies the statutory requirement, irrespective of delayed bond allotment (*Hindustan Unilever Ltd. v. DCIT*).

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Section 50C Safe Harbour Rule:** If the Stamp Duty Value does not exceed **110% of the actual consideration**, the actual consideration received is taken as the Full Value of Consideration.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Taxation of Mutual Funds Capital Gains & Section 54F Exemption Framework
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Mutual Funds & Section 54F

| Category | Fund Criteria | Acquisition Date | Holding Threshold | Asset & Tax Nature |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Equity Oriented Fund** | Equity Exposure ≥ 65% | Any Date | > 12 Months | **LTCG** u/s 112A |
| **Equity Oriented Fund** | Equity Exposure ≥ 65% | Any Date | ≤ 12 Months | **STCG** u/s 111A |
| **Specified Mutual Fund** | Equity Exposure ≤ 35% | On/After 1st April 2023 | Irrelevant | **Deemed STCA** u/s 50AA |
| **Debt Mutual Fund** | Equity Exposure < 65% | Before 1st April 2023 | > 36 Months / 24 Months | **LTCG** u/s 112 |


### Core Statutory Conditions

* **Section 50AA Deemed Short-Term Treatment**: Specified Mutual Funds (where investment in domestic equity shares is not more than 35%) acquired on or after 1st April 2023 are deemed to be Short-Term Capital Assets irrespective of period of holding.

* **Section 54F Scope & Requisite Criteria**: Exemption is available **ONLY** against Long-Term Capital Gains arising from transfer of any long-term capital asset other than a residential house, provided investment is made in one residential house in India within 1 year before or 2 years after transfer.


### Proportional Exemption Formula u/s 54F

$$\text{Exemption Amount} = \text{Long-Term Capital Gain} \times \left( \frac{\text{Cost of New Residential House}}{\text{Net Sale Consideration}} \right)$$


> [!WARNING] Section 54F Allocation Trap: Short-Term Capital Gains (including Section 50AA deemed STCG) are completely ineligible for Section 54F exemption. When multiple LTCG assets are sold, the new house investment is allocated sequentially up to the net consideration of each LTCG asset.

provisions.subject: dt
provisions.topic_title: Section 54G: Exemption on Shifting Industrial Undertaking from Urban to Non-Urban Area & Interplay with Section 50
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
### Statutory Summary Matrix: Shifting of Industrial Undertaking u/s 54G & Deemed STCG u/s 50

| Provision / Section | Eligible Assets / Scope | Time Limit for Reinvestment | Statutory Tax Treatment & Optimization |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Section 54G** | Plant, Machinery, Land, Building (used for industrial undertaking) | 1 Year before OR 3 Years after transfer date | Exempt up to cost of new assets; excess CG taxable u/s 45 |
| **Ineligible Assets u/s 54G** | Furniture, fittings, general office equipment | Not Applicable | **No Section 54G exemption** available for furniture |
| **Section 50** | Depreciable assets (Plant, Machinery, Building, Furniture) | Cost deemed as WDV of block | Capital gain treated as **Deemed Short-Term Capital Gain** |
| **Tax Optimization Rule** | Set-off priority of Section 54G exemption | Simultaneous LTCG & STCG availability | Set-off first against **STCG** (higher tax rate), balance against **LTCG** |


### Core Statutory Conditions Checklist

* **Eligible Transfer & Shifting Trigger:** Transfer must occur in the course of, or in consequence of, shifting an industrial undertaking from an urban area to a non-urban area.
* **Qualifying Reinvestment Avenues:** Acquisition of new plant/machinery, land/building, construction of building, or shifting expenses of existing establishment to the non-urban area.
* **Restriction on Furniture:** Capital gains arising on furniture transfer do not qualify for Section 54G exemption, nor does acquiring furniture count as qualifying reinvestment.
* **Exemption Priority Rule:** Where an assessee has both STCG (u/s 50) and LTCG (non-depreciable land), the Section 54G exemption must first be set off against STCG to maximize tax relief.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Mandatory Priority Rule: Because Short-Term Capital Gain under Section 50 is taxed at normal applicable rates whereas Long-Term Capital Gain is taxed at concessional rates under Section 112, the assessee is legally entitled to exhaust Section 54G exemption against Short-Term Capital Gains first.

provisions.topic_title: Section 112A: Tax on Long-Term Capital Gains & Grandfathering Mechanism
provisions.provision_presentation_markdown:
| Asset Type | STT Condition | FMV as on 31st January 2018 | Tax Rate u/s 112A | Annual Threshold |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Listed Equity Shares** | Paid on both Acquisition & Transfer | Highest trading price on recognized stock exchange on 31.01.2018 | 12.5% + Cess | First ₹ 1,25,000 Exempt |
| **Equity Oriented Fund Units** | Paid on Transfer | Highest trading price (if listed on 31.01.2018) OR Net Asset Value (if unlisted on 31.01.2018) | 12.5% + Cess | First ₹ 1,25,000 Exempt |

**Statutory Grandfathering Cost Formula (Assets Acquired Before 01.02.2018):**
- **Cost of Acquisition** = **Higher of (A) and (B)**
  - **(A)** Actual Cost of Acquisition
  - **(B)** **Lower of**:
    - Fair Market Value (FMV) as on 31st January 2018
    - Full Value of Consideration (Actual Sale Consideration)

> [!IMPORTANT] Pre-2018 Gain Protection: The grandfathering mechanism ensures that any capital gains accrued prior to 1st February 2018 are completely grandfathered and shielded from Direct Tax.

> [!WARNING] Unlisted Asset Benchmark Trap: If a unit or share was unlisted as on 31st January 2018, its FMV MUST be taken as the Net Asset Value (NAV) on 31st January 2018, even if it gets listed on a stock exchange prior to the date of transfer.

root.title: Diversion vs Application of Income
root.voice_sync_text: നമസ്കാരം! ഇന്ന് നമ്മൾ CA Final Direct Tax-ലെ വളരെ പ്രധാനപ്പെട്ട ഒരു ജുഡീഷ്യൽ ഡോക്ട്രിൻ ആണ് പഠിക്കുന്നത് - Diversion of Income by Overriding Title versus Application of Income. ഒരു വരുമാനം നികുതിദായകന്റെ കൈകളിൽ ടാക്സ് ചെയ്യപ്പെടേണ്ടതുണ്ടോ എന്ന് തീരുമാനിക്കുന്നതിൽ ഈ തത്വം വളരെ നിർണ്ണായകമാണ്.

points.title: Diversion by Overriding Title
body: Obligation attaches directly to the source of income before it reaches the assessee
Income is diverted at source to a third party under an enforceable paramount title
Excluded from total income computation of the assessee
points.voice_sync_text: Diversion of income എന്ന് പറഞ്ഞാൽ, വരുമാനത്തിന്റെ സോഴ്സിൽ തന്നെ ഒരു ഓവർറൈഡിംഗ് ലീഗൽ ഒബ്ലിഗേഷൻ ഉണ്ടാവുകയും, അത് അസ്സസ്സിയുടെ കൈകളിൽ എത്തുന്നതിന് മുൻപ് തന്നെ മൂന്നാമതൊരാളിലേക്ക് വഴിതിരിച്ചു വിടപ്പെടുകയും ചെയ്യുകയാണ്. ഇത് അസ്സസ്സിയുടെ ടോട്ടൽ ഇൻകത്തിൽ ഉൾപ്പെടില്ല.

points.title: Application of Income
body: Income reaches or accrues to the assessee first as their property
Subsequently applied to discharge an obligation, personal debt, or contractual commitment
Fully taxable in the hands of the assessee
points.voice_sync_text: എന്നാൽ Application of income-ൽ, വരുമാനം ആദ്യം അസ്സസ്സിക്ക് അക്രൂ ചെയ്യുകയോ കൈകളിൽ എത്തുകയോ ചെയ്യുന്നു. അതിനുശേഷമാണ് അത് മറ്റെന്തെങ്കിലും ബാധ്യത തീർക്കാൻ ചിലവഴിക്കുന്നത്. അതിനാൽ ഇത് അസ്സസ്സിയുടെ കൈകളിൽ പൂർണ്ണമായും ടാക്സബിൾ ആണ്.

points.title: Key Legal Criteria
body: Time of attachment: Before accrual vs After accrual
Nature of title: Paramount title on source vs Personal covenant

rows: Assessee has no right to receive

points.voice_sync_text: ഈ രണ്ട് സങ്കൽപ്പങ്ങളും തമ്മിലുള്ള വ്യത്യാസം കാണിക്കുന്ന ടേബിൾ ശ്രദ്ധിക്കൂ. ഇൻകം എവിടെ വെച്ചാണ് കൈമാറ്റം ചെയ്യപ്പെടുന്നത് എന്നതാണ് പ്രധാന മാനദണ്ഡം. അക്രൂവലിന് മുൻപെങ്കിൽ Diversion, അക്രൂവലിന് ശേഷമെങ്കിൽ Application.

points.title: Jit & Pal X-Rays (P.) Ltd. Ratio
body: Overriding charge embedded in the sale deed for acquiring sole proprietorship
Condition of purchase explicitly charged ₹ 15,000 p.a. on net profits to proprietor's wife
Obligation attached to the very source of income transferred
Held: Diversion of income by overriding title; not taxable in assessee's hands
points.voice_sync_text: അലഹാബാദ് ഹൈക്കോടതിയുടെ Jit and Pal X-Rays കേസിൽ, ഒരു സോളെ പ്രൊപ്രൈറ്റർഷിപ്പ് ബിസിനസ്സ് വാങ്ങുമ്പോൾ തന്നെ സെയിൽ ഡീഡിൽ ഒരു കണ്ടീഷൻ വെയ്ക്കുന്നു - അവിടുത്തെ നെറ്റ് പ്രോഫിറ്റിൽ നിന്നും പ്രൊപ്രൈറ്ററുടെ ഭാര്യക്ക് 15,000 രൂപ പ്രതിവർഷം നൽകണം. ഈ ബാധ്യത ബിസിനസ്സ് വാങ്ങുന്നതിന്റെ സോഴ്സിനോട് തന്നെ ഘടിപ്പിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നതിനാൽ, ഇത് Diversion of Income ആണ് എന്ന് കോടതി വിധി എഴുതി.

points.title: Steps to Determine Tax Liability
body: Check 1: Was the charge created simultaneously with or prior to acquiring the asset?
Check 2: Is the charge enforceable against the source itself?
If YES to both -> Diversion (Exclude from income). If NO -> Application (Include in income).
points.voice_sync_text: പരീക്ഷയിൽ ചോദ്യം വരുമ്പോൾ രണ്ട് കാര്യങ്ങൾ പരിശോധിക്കുക: ഒന്ന്, ഇൻകം സോഴ്സ് സ്വന്തമാക്കുന്ന ആ നിമിഷത്തിൽ തന്നെയാണോ ബാധ്യത ഉണ്ടായത്? രണ്ട്, അത് പ്രസ്തുത സോഴ്സിൽ നേരിട്ടുള്ള ചാർജ്ജ് ആണോ? ഈ രണ്ട് ചോദ്യങ്ങൾക്കും ഉത്തരം യെസ് എന്നാണെങ്കിൽ അത് Diversion of income ആയിരിക്കും.

root.title: Diversion vs Application of Income
root.voice_sync_text: നമസ്കാരം! ഇന്ന് നമ്മൾ CA Final Direct Tax-ലെ വളരെ പ്രധാനപ്പെട്ട ഒരു ജുഡീഷ്യൽ ഡോക്ട്രിൻ ആണ് പഠിക്കുന്നത് - Diversion of Income by Overriding Title versus Application of Income. ഒരു വരുമാനം നികുതിദായകന്റെ കൈകളിൽ ടാക്സ് ചെയ്യപ്പെടേണ്ടതുണ്ടോ എന്ന് തീരുമാനിക്കുന്നതിൽ ഈ തത്വം വളരെ നിർണ്ണായകമാണ്.

points.title: Diversion by Overriding Title
body: Obligation attaches directly to the source of income before it reaches the assessee
Income is diverted at source to a third party under an enforceable paramount title
Excluded from total income computation of the assessee
points.voice_sync_text: Diversion of income എന്ന് പറഞ്ഞാൽ, വരുമാനത്തിന്റെ സോഴ്സിൽ തന്നെ ഒരു ഓവർറൈഡിംഗ് ലീഗൽ ഒബ്ലിഗേഷൻ ഉണ്ടാവുകയും, അത് അസ്സസ്സിയുടെ കൈകളിൽ എത്തുന്നതിന് മുൻപ് തന്നെ മൂന്നാമതൊരാളിലേക്ക് വഴിതിരിച്ചു വിടപ്പെടുകയും ചെയ്യുകയാണ്. ഇത് അസ്സസ്സിയുടെ ടോട്ടൽ ഇൻകത്തിൽ ഉൾപ്പെടില്ല.

points.title: Application of Income
body: Income reaches or accrues to the assessee first as their property
Subsequently applied to discharge an obligation, personal debt, or contractual commitment
Fully taxable in the hands of the assessee
points.voice_sync_text: എന്നാൽ Application of income-ൽ, വരുമാനം ആദ്യം അസ്സസ്സിക്ക് അക്രൂ ചെയ്യുകയോ കൈകളിൽ എത്തുകയോ ചെയ്യുന്നു. അതിനുശേഷമാണ് അത് മറ്റെന്തെങ്കിലും ബാധ്യത തീർക്കാൻ ചിലവഴിക്കുന്നത്. അതിനാൽ ഇത് അസ്സസ്സിയുടെ കൈകളിൽ പൂർണ്ണമായും ടാക്സബിൾ ആണ്.

points.title: Key Legal Criteria
body: Time of attachment: Before accrual vs After accrual
Nature of title: Paramount title on source vs Personal covenant

rows: Assessee has no right to receive

points.voice_sync_text: ഈ രണ്ട് സങ്കൽപ്പങ്ങളും തമ്മിലുള്ള വ്യത്യാസം കാണിക്കുന്ന ടേബിൾ ശ്രദ്ധിക്കൂ. ഇൻകം എവിടെ വെച്ചാണ് കൈമാറ്റം ചെയ്യപ്പെടുന്നത് എന്നതാണ് പ്രധാന മാനദണ്ഡം. അക്രൂവലിന് മുൻപെങ്കിൽ Diversion, അക്രൂവലിന് ശേഷമെങ്കിൽ Application.

points.title: Jit & Pal X-Rays (P.) Ltd. Ratio
body: Overriding charge embedded in the sale deed for acquiring sole proprietorship
Condition of purchase explicitly charged ₹ 15,000 p.a. on net profits to proprietor's wife
Obligation attached to the very source of income transferred
Held: Diversion of income by overriding title; not taxable in assessee's hands
points.voice_sync_text: അലഹാബാദ് ഹൈക്കോടതിയുടെ Jit and Pal X-Rays കേസിൽ, ഒരു സോളെ പ്രൊപ്രൈറ്റർഷിപ്പ് ബിസിനസ്സ് വാങ്ങുമ്പോൾ തന്നെ സെയിൽ ഡീഡിൽ ഒരു കണ്ടീഷൻ വെയ്ക്കുന്നു - അവിടുത്തെ നെറ്റ് പ്രോഫിറ്റിൽ നിന്നും പ്രൊപ്രൈറ്ററുടെ ഭാര്യക്ക് 15,000 രൂപ പ്രതിവർഷം നൽകണം. ഈ ബാധ്യത ബിസിനസ്സ് വാങ്ങുന്നതിന്റെ സോഴ്സിനോട് തന്നെ ഘടിപ്പിച്ചിരിക്കുന്നതിനാൽ, ഇത് Diversion of Income ആണ് എന്ന് കോടതി വിധി എഴുതി.

points.title: Steps to Determine Tax Liability
body: Check 1: Was the charge created simultaneously with or prior to acquiring the asset?
Check 2: Is the charge enforceable against the source itself?
If YES to both -> Diversion (Exclude from income). If NO -> Application (Include in income).
points.voice_sync_text: പരീക്ഷയിൽ ചോദ്യം വരുമ്പോൾ രണ്ട് കാര്യങ്ങൾ പരിശോധിക്കുക: ഒന്ന്, ഇൻകം സോഴ്സ് സ്വന്തമാക്കുന്ന ആ നിമിഷത്തിൽ തന്നെയാണോ ബാധ്യത ഉണ്ടായത്? രണ്ട്, അത് പ്രസ്തുത സോഴ്സിൽ നേരിട്ടുള്ള ചാർജ്ജ് ആണോ? ഈ രണ്ട് ചോദ്യങ്ങൾക്കും ഉത്തരം യെസ് എന്നാണെങ്കിൽ അത് Diversion of income ആയിരിക്കും.

ch1_q3.doctrine: Diversion of Income by Overriding Title vs Application of Income

root.title: Diversion vs Application of Income
root.voice_sync_text: ഇന്ന് നമ്മൾ പഠിക്കുന്നത് Direct Tax-ലെ ഏറ്റവും പ്രധാനപ്പെട്ട ഒരു Judicial Doctrine ആയ Diversion of Income by Overriding Title-നെക്കുറിച്ചാണ്. Income അസ്സസ്സിക്ക് ലഭിക്കുന്നതിന് മുൻപ് തന്നെ legal obligation വഴി diverted ആകുകയാണോ, അതോ ലഭിച്ച ശേഷം ചെലവഴിക്കുകയാണോ (Application of Income) എന്ന് തിരിച്ചറിയുന്നത് taxability നിർണ്ണയിക്കാൻ വളരെ അത്യാവശ്യമാണ്.

points.title: Diversion at Source (Overriding Title)
body: Income is intercepted BEFORE it accrues to or reaches the assessee.
Source of income is inherently burdened with a legal obligation or charge.
Assessee receives the money merely as a conduit/trustee for the actual beneficiary.
Result: Excluded from total income of the assessee.
points.voice_sync_text: Diversion of Income by Overriding Title എന്ന് പറയുമ്പോൾ, വരുമാനം അസ്സസ്സിയുടെ കൈകളിൽ എത്തുന്നതിന് മുൻപ് തന്നെ ഒരു legal charge വഴി മറ്റൊരാളിലേക്ക് തടഞ്ഞുമാറ്റപ്പെടുന്നു. ഇവിടെ അസ്സസ്സി ഒരു conduit അല്ലെങ്കിൽ agent മാത്രമാണ്. അതിനാൽ ഈ തുക അസ്സസ്സിയുടെ taxable income-ൽ നിന്ന് ഒഴിവാക്കണം.

points.title: Application of Income
body: Income accrues to or reaches the assessee FIRST.
Subsequently spent or applied by the assessee to meet personal or contractual obligations.
Title to the income resides fully with the assessee at the point of accrual.
Result: Fully taxable in the hands of the assessee.
points.voice_sync_text: എന്നാൽ Application of Income-ൽ വരുമാനം ആദ്യം അസ്സസ്സിക്ക് ലഭിക്കുകയോ accrue ചെയ്യുകയോ ചെയ്യുന്നു. അതിനുശേഷമാണ് അസ്സസ്സി സ്വന്തം ഇഷ്ടപ്രകാരമോ മറ്റൊരു കരാർ അനുസരിച്ചോ അത് ചെലവഴിക്കുന്നത്. അതിനാൽ ഈ തുകയ്ക്ക് അസ്സസ്സി പൂർണ്ണമായും Tax നൽകേണ്ടതുണ്ട്.

points.title: CIT v. Sitaldas Tirathdas (SC Test)
body: True test: Is the obligation to apply income which has accrued, or is it an obligation to divert income before it reaches the assessee?
If the obligation binds the source directly, it is Diversion by Overriding Title.
points.voice_sync_text: CIT v. Sitaldas Tirathdas കേസിൽ സുപ്രീം കോടതി നൽകിയ പ്രശസ്തമായ ടെസ്റ്റ് ഇതാണ്: വരുമാനം ലഭിച്ച ശേഷമാണോ അത് ചിലവഴിക്കാൻ obligation ഉള്ളത്, അതോ അസ്സസ്സിക്ക് ലഭിക്കുന്നതിന് മുൻപ് തന്നെ source-നെ ബാധിക്കുന്ന obligation ആണോ? Source-നെയാണ് ബാധിക്കുന്നതെങ്കിൽ അത് Diversion ആണ്.

points.title: Deed Covenant & Creation of Charge
body: Partnership deed provided business continuation after father's death subject to paying 20% profits to mother.
Condition precedent creates a legal charge over the profit-earning capacity of the reconstituted firm.
Mother holds an overriding title superior to the reconstituted firm for that 20% share.
points.voice_sync_text: ഇനി നമ്മൾ വിശകലനം ചെയ്ത ചോദ്യത്തിലേക്ക് വരാം. Partnership deed-ൽ അച്ഛന്റെ മരണശേഷം മക്കൾക്ക് ബിസിനസ്സ് തുടർന്ന് നടത്താം, പക്ഷെ ലാഭത്തിന്റെ 20 ശതമാനം അമ്മയ്ക്ക് നൽകണം എന്ന് കൃത്യമായി പറഞ്ഞിട്ടുണ്ട്. ഈ condition ബിസിനസ്സ് തുടരാനുള്ള ഒരു prerequisite ആയതുകൊണ്ട് അമ്മയ്ക്ക് അതിൽ overriding title ഉണ്ട്.

points.title: Taxability & Correctness of Claim
body: Firm received the ₹1 lakh (20% profit) for and on behalf of the mother.
Claim of the firm to exclude/deduct ₹1 lakh from its taxable income is legally CORRECT.
Precedent: CIT v. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons (1981) 130 ITR 863 (Bom).
points.voice_sync_text: അതുകൊണ്ട്, ബോംബെ ഹൈക്കോടതിയുടെ CIT vs. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons വിധി പ്രകാരം, 20% ലാഭമായ ഒരു ലക്ഷം രൂപ firm അമ്മയ്ക്ക് വേണ്ടി കൈപ്പറ്റിയതാണ്. അത് firm-ന്റെ வருമാനമല്ല. Firm അത് income-ൽ നിന്ന് exclude ചെയ്തത് പൂർണ്ണമായും ശരിയാണ്.

points.title: Decision Checklist for Diversion vs Application
body: Check origin of obligation: Pre-existing instrument/deed or post-accrual decision?
Check nature of title: Does third party have superior claim enforcing overriding title?
Check receipt status: Is money received as absolute owner or as conduit?

rows: CIT v. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons

points.voice_sync_text: പരീക്ഷയിൽ ഇത്തരം ചോദ്യങ്ങൾ വന്നാൽ എളുപ്പത്തിൽ മനസ്സിലാക്കാൻ ഈ checklist ഓർക്കുക: Obligation എപ്പോൾ ഉണ്ടെന്നു നോക്കുക, Third party-ക്ക് legal right ഉണ്ടോ എന്ന് നോക്കുക. Pre-existing charge ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ Diversion, അതുകൊണ്ട് Taxable total income-ൽ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തില്ല.

points.voice_sync_text: അതുകൊണ്ട്, ബോംബെ ഹൈക്കോടതിയുടെ CIT vs. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons വിധി പ്രകാരം, 20% ലാഭമായ ഒരു ലക്ഷം രൂപ firm അമ്മയ്ക്ക് വേണ്ടി കൈപ്പറ്റിയതാണ്. അത് firm-ന്റെ வருമാനമല്ല. Firm അത് income-ൽ നിന്ന് exclude ചെയ്തത് പൂർണ്ണമായും ശരിയാണ്.

points.title: Decision Checklist for Diversion vs Application
body: Check origin of obligation: Pre-existing instrument/deed or post-accrual decision?
Check nature of title: Does third party have superior claim enforcing overriding title?
Check receipt status: Is money received as absolute owner or as conduit?

rows: CIT v. Nariman B. Bharucha & Sons

points.voice_sync_text: പരീക്ഷയിൽ ഇത്തരം ചോദ്യങ്ങൾ വന്നാൽ എളുപ്പത്തിൽ മനസ്സിലാക്കാൻ ഈ checklist ഓർക്കുക: Obligation എപ്പോൾ ഉണ്ടെന്നു നോക്കുക, Third party-ക്ക് legal right ഉണ്ടോ എന്ന് നോക്കുക. Pre-existing charge ഉണ്ടെങ്കിൽ Diversion, അതുകൊണ്ട് Taxable total income-ൽ ഉൾപ്പെടുത്തില്ല.

ch1_q4.doctrine: Old Tax Regime Slab Rates & Age Tiers

root.title: Old Tax Regime Individual Tax Slabs
root.voice_sync_text: നമസ്കാരം, ഇന്ന് നമ്മൾ പഠിക്കുന്നത് 115BAC ഒപ്റ്റ് ഔട്ട് ചെയ്ത് ഓൾഡ് ടാക്സ് റെജീമിൽ ഒരു ഇൻഡിവിജ്വലിന്റെ ടാക്സ് ലയബിലിറ്റി കണക്കാക്കുന്ന രീതിയാണ്. വയസ്സ് അനുസരിച്ച് മൂന്ന് തരം Basic Exemption Limits ഇവിടെ ലഭ്യമാണ്.

points.title: Normal Individual Tax Slabs
body: Applicable to resident individuals aged below 60 years and all Non-Residents.
Basic Exemption Limit (BEL) is ₹ 2,50,000.
points.voice_sync_text: ആദ്യത്തെ വിഭാഗം അറുപത് വയസ്സിന് താഴെയുള്ള റെസിഡന്റ് ഇൻഡിവിജ്വൽസും, വയസ്സ് എത്രയായാലും ഉള്ള എല്ലാ നോൺ-റെസിഡന്റ്സുമാണ്. ഇവർക്ക് Basic Exemption Limit രണ്ടര ലക്ഷം രൂപയാണ്. രണ്ടര മുതൽ അഞ്ച് ലക്ഷം വരെ അഞ്ച് ശതമാനം, അഞ്ച് മുതൽ പത്ത് ലക്ഷം വരെ ഇരുപത് ശതമാനം, പത്ത് ലക്ഷത്തിന് മുകളിൽ മുപ്പത് ശതമാനവുമാണ് ടാക്സ് നിരക്ക്.

points.title: Senior Citizen Slab Structure
body: Applicable ONLY to Resident individuals who are 60 years or older but below 80 years during the P.Y.
Basic Exemption Limit (BEL) is enhanced to ₹ 3,00,000.
First 5% slab compressed to ₹ 2,00,000 (from ₹ 3,00,001 to ₹ 5,00,000).
points.voice_sync_text: രണ്ടാമത്തെ വിഭാഗം 60 മുതൽ 79 വയസ്സ് വരെയുള്ള റെസിഡന്റ് സീനിയർ സിറ്റിസൺസാണ്. ഇവർക്ക് Basic Exemption Limit മൂന്ന് ലക്ഷം രൂപയാണ്. അതിനാൽ ആദ്യത്തെ അഞ്ച് ശതമാനം സ്ലാബിൽ വരുന്നത് മൂന്ന് ലക്ഷം മുതൽ അഞ്ച് ലക്ഷം വരെയുള്ള രണ്ട് ലക്ഷം രൂപ മാത്രമാണ്, അതായത് പരമാവധി 10,000 രൂപ.

branches.branch_title: Category III: Resident Super Senior Citizens (Age 80+)

points.title: Super Senior Citizen Slab Structure
body: Applicable ONLY to Resident individuals aged 80 years or more during the P.Y.
Basic Exemption Limit (BEL) is elevated to ₹ 5,00,000.
5% tax slab is completely ELIMINATED for Super Senior Citizens.
points.voice_sync_text: മൂന്നാമത്തെ വിഭാഗം 80 വയസ്സോ അതിൽ കൂടുതലോ ഉള്ള റെസിഡന്റ് സൂപ്പർ സീനിയർ സിറ്റിസൺസാണ്. ഇവർക്ക് അഞ്ച് ലക്ഷം രൂപ വരെ ടാക്സ് തീരെയില്ല! ഇവിടെ 5% എന്ന ടാക്സ് സ്ലാബ് തികച്ചും ഒഴിവാക്കപ്പെട്ടിരിക്കുന്നു. അഞ്ച് ലക്ഷത്തിന് മുകളിലുള്ള തുകയ്ക്ക് നേരിട്ട് 20% നിരക്കിലാണ് ടാക്സ് ആരംഭിക്കുന്നത്.

points.title: Health & Education Cess Addition
body: Compute basic tax on total income based on the applicable age slab.
Add Health and Education Cess @ 4% on the total basic tax (plus surcharge if applicable).
Resultant figure is the final rounded-off tax liability.
points.voice_sync_text: അവസാനമായി, ടോട്ടൽ ഇൻകം സ്ലാബ് പ്രകാരം കണക്കാക്കിയ ബേസിക് ടാക്സ് തുകയുടെ കൂടെ നാല് ശതമാനം Health and Education Cess നിർബന്ധമായും കൂട്ടണം. ഇതാണ് ടാക്സ് പേയറുടെ ഫൈനൽ ടാക്സ് ലയബിലിറ്റി.

ch1_q5.doctrine: Old Tax Regime Individual Tax Slabs & Section 87A Rebate

root.title: Old Tax Regime Slabs & Sec 87A Rebate
root.voice_sync_text: നമസ്കാരം, ഇന്ന് നമ്മൾ പഠിക്കുന്നത് ന്യൂ ടാക്സ് റെജീമിൽ നിന്ന് മാറി ഓൾഡ് ടാക്സ് റെജീം തെരഞ്ഞെടുക്കുമ്പോൾ ഇൻഡിവ്വിജ്വൽ അസ്സസ്സീകൾക്കുള്ള ടാക്സ് സ്ലാബുകളും സെക്ഷൻ 87A പ്രകാരമുള്ള റിബേറ്റുമാണ്.

points.title: Shift-Out Option Mechanics
body: Section 115BAC is the default regime for individuals.
Assessee can opt out under Sec 115BAC(6) to be governed by normal provisions.
Non-business assessees can exercise this option annually upon filing ITR.
points.voice_sync_text: സെക്ഷൻ 115BAC ആണ് ഇപ്പോൾ ഡിഫോൾട്ട് ടാക്സ് റെജീം. എന്നാൽ ഒരു അസ്സസ്സീക്ക് സെക്ഷൻ 115BAC സബ്സെക്ഷൻ 6 പ്രകാരം ഓൾഡ് ടാക്സ് റെജീമിലേക്ക് ഒപ്റ്റ് ഔട്ട് ചെയ്യാം. ബിസിനസ് ഇൻകം ഇല്ലാത്തവർക്ക് ഓരോ വർഷവും റിട്ടേൺ ഫയൽ ചെയ്യുമ്പോൾ ഈ ഓപ്ഷൻ മാറ്റാവുന്നതാണ്.

points.title: Progressive Slab Architecture
body: Basic Exemption Limit (BEL) is ₹ 2,50,000 for individuals below 60 years.
Income between ₹ 2.5L and ₹ 5L is taxed at 5%.
Health and Education Cess @ 4% applies on tax post-rebate.
points.voice_sync_text: 60 വയസ്സിന് താഴെയുള്ള റെസിഡന്റ് ഇൻഡിവ്വിജ്വലിന് ഓൾഡ് റെജീമിൽ ബേസിക് എക്സംപ്ഷൻ ലിമിറ്റ് 2,50,000 രൂപയാണ്. 2,50,000 മുതൽ 5 ലക്ഷം വരെയുള്ള വരുമാനത്തിന് 5 ശതമാനമാണ് ടാക്സ് നിരക്ക്.

points.title: Statutory Eligibility & Monetary Cap
body: Applicable ONLY to Resident Individuals.
Total Income must NOT exceed ₹ 5,00,000 in Old Regime.
Maximum rebate limit is ₹ 12,500 (or 100% of tax, whichever is lower).
points.voice_sync_text: സെക്ഷൻ 87A റിബേറ്റ് ലഭിക്കാൻ പ്രധാനമായും മൂന്ന് വ്യവസ്ഥകളുണ്ട്. ഒന്നാമതായി അസ്സസ്സീ റെസിഡന്റ് ഇൻഡിവ്വിജ്വൽ ആയിരിക്കണം. രണ്ടാമതായി ടോട്ടൽ ഇൻകം 5 ലക്ഷം രൂപയിൽ കൂടരുത്. പരമാവധി ലഭിക്കുന്ന റിബേറ്റ് 12,500 രൂപ അല്ലെങ്കിൽ ഇൻകം ടാക്സ് തുക, ഇതിൽ കുറവേതോ അതാണ്.

points.title: Exceptions & Exclusions
body: Non-residents are completely ineligible for Sec 87A rebate.
Tax on LTCG u/s 112A cannot be offset against Sec 87A rebate.
points.voice_sync_text: ശ്രദ്ധിക്കേണ്ട ഒരു കാര്യം, നോൺ-റെസിഡന്റുകൾക്ക് സെക്ഷൻ 87A റിബേറ്റ് ലഭിക്കില്ല. കൂടാതെ സെക്ഷൻ 112A പ്രകാരമുള്ള ലോങ് ടേം ക്യാപിറ്റൽ ഗെയിൻസിന് മേലുള്ള ടാക്സിന് എതിരായി 87A റിബേറ്റ് അഡ്ജസ്റ്റ് ചെയ്യാൻ കഴിയില്ല.
